AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 2, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION  PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9(D)(4) – Initiation of litigation in one matter.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Property: Assessor Property Numbers 8056-015-014 and 8056-025-020; Negotiating
  Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the City and Primestor Development Inc.; Under
  Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Abey Joseph
  Rock of the Nations

FLAG SALUTE
  Jasmin Perez
  Norwalk High School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  City Council to recognize the winners of the Home and Business Beautification Program.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Keepin’ it Norwalk: Business Spotlight video.

  3.  Mini Mr. Sun Clean-Up Program video.

  4.  Summer Concerts and Front Street Friday Night’s video.

  5.  Bi-Weekly Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR
 Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of July 19,
  2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period July 10, 2022 – July 23,
  2022, in the total amount of $1,202,709.59. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period July
  12, through July 25, 2022 in the total amount of $5,438,598.07. 640

  Warrant Register

  4.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – JULY 27, 2022 - No action is required unless the City Council
  elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the Commission’s
  action was final. 320

  Report

  5.  PROJECT NO. 7930 - ACCEPT WORK FOR COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT
  FUNDED LOCAL STREET REHABILITATION IN ZONE 28 – ENGINEERS REPORT 22-19 - Staff
  recommends City Council accept the work of All American Asphalt in the amount of $1,072,922 for the
  Community Development Block Grant Local Streets Rehabilitation Project. 1005-04-7930

  Report

  6.  PROJECT NO. 3302-2223 - RESOLUTION NO. 22-45 – BUDGET AMENDMENT AND AWARD OF
  CONTRACT FOR ANNUAL CITYWIDE SIDEWALK CONCRETE REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT,
  ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 22-17 – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-45, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE MEASURE R BOND FUNDS AND TRANSPORTATION
  DEVELOPMENT ACT ARTICLE 3 FUNDS FOR AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT CURB
  RAMP INSTALLATIONS TO PROJECT NO. 3302-2223 - ANNUAL CITYWIDE SIDEWALK
  CONCRETE REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT, in the amounts of $98,740 and $67,000 respectively;
  and

  b.  award a contract to CJ Concrete Construction of Santa Fe Springs in the amount of $423,400 for
  Project No. 3302-2223, citywide sidewalk concrete repair and replacement; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the agreement and any extension/amendments including potential change
  orders, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney.
  1005-04-3302-2223

  Report

  7.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING – PROPOSITION C 5% TRANSIT SECURITY FUNDS - Staff
  recommends City Council approve the Memorandum of Understanding with the Los Angeles County
  Metropolitan Transportation Authority for the use of Proposition C 5% Security Funds from July 1, 2022
  through June 30, 2027, in the amount of $151,822 for Fiscal Year 2022/23; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the Memorandum of Understanding on behalf of City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney. 1105-02

  Report

  8.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING – PROPOSITION C 40% DISCRETIONARY PROGRAM
  FUNDS - Staff recommends City Council approve the Memorandum of Understanding with the Los
  Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority for the use of Proposition C 40% Discretionary
   funds from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2032, in the amount of $212,140 for Fiscal Year 2022/23; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the Memorandum of Understanding on behalf of City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. 1105-02

  Report

  9.  APPROVAL OF PARCEL MAP NO. 82718; A LOT MERGER OF CITY OWNED PROPERTY AT THE
  SOUTHWEST CORNER OF SAN ANTONIO DRIVE AND FOSTER ROAD, ENGINEER’S REPORT
  NO. 22-18 - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  authorize the merger of the City owned properties at the southwest corner of San Antonio Drive
  and Foster Road, and reserve an easement for future emergency access and fire lane purposes
  as indicated on proposed Parcel Map No. 82718;

  b.  approve Parcel Map No. 82718. 320-14-82718

  Report

  10. AGREEMENT FOR ZERO EMISSIONS BUS ROLLOUT PLAN - Staff recommends City Council
  approve a professional services agreement with Stantec Consulting Services, Inc. in an amount not to
  exceed $99,228 from August 3, 2022 through June 30, 2023, and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget and it is within the
  City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

  11. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 4 – ON-CALL BUILDING & SAFETY AND PLANNING
  CONSULTING SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 4 to the
  agreement with CSG Consultants, Inc. to provide on-call professional building and planning consultant
  services in an amount not to exceed $316,000; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and any additional amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the
  City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 300

  Report

  12. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT – HEALTH ON WHEELS PROGRAM – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  approve an amendment to the agreement with the Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School District and
  California State University Long Beach Foundation to provide free and accessible basic health
  care services to children in the Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School District from July 1, 2022
  through September 30, 2022; and

  b.  approve an amendment to the Bailment agreement with the Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School
  District, for storage of a motor home vehicle at the Norwalk City Yard from July 1, 2022 through
  September 30, 2022; and

  c.  authorize the City Manager to execute both amendments, on behalf of the City, in forms approved
  by the City Attorney. 440

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  13. ADVISORY BODIES - Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

RESOLUTION

  14. NEW JOB CLASSIFICATIONS AND RESOLUTION NO. 22-46 - APPROVING A REVISED FISCAL
  YEAR 2022/23 SALARY SCHEDULE – Staff recommends City Council approve the new classifications
  and adopt Resolution No. 22-46, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AMENDING THE SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 FOR THE
   GENERAL, HOURLY, AND EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT AND MID-MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES.
  135-03

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated July 29, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
